blocks.text: What is cloud hosting, in simple words

content.text: Cloud hosting is a way of running a website on a pool of connected servers instead of a single physical server. Your website, its files and its database live on virtual resources drawn from that pool. If one server in the pool has a problem, your site can keep running from another one. If your site suddenly gets more visitors, more resources can be added without moving the site to a different server.

The word cloud is used for many things, but for hosting it has a practical meaning. You get a hosting account with a set amount of CPU, RAM and storage, just like other hosting, except the resources come from a network rather than one machine. From your side, nothing feels unusual: you still get cPanel, you still upload files and install WordPress the same way, and visitors still open your domain in a browser.

A cloud platform keeps many physical servers working together as one system. Your website runs in a virtual container on that system, with its own CPU, RAM and storage. The platform watches the health of the hardware underneath. If a physical server fails, the container can restart on healthy hardware with its data intact, because storage is copied across more than one drive or machine. That is the failover that gives cloud hosting its reputation for staying online.

Scaling works the same way. When traffic rises, the plan can give your site more CPU or RAM. When traffic falls again, you are not stuck paying for capacity you no longer use. Compare that with a single-server setup, where an upgrade usually means moving the whole site to a bigger machine.

blocks.text: Cloud hosting vs shared hosting vs VPS

content.text: The three types solve different problems. Shared hosting suits most new websites. A VPS suits sites that need their own server space and more control. Cloud hosting suits sites that need room to grow and high availability. See
shared hosting vs VPS hosting in Pakistan
for the shared and VPS side of this comparison in detail.

blocks.text: 1. Your site slows down at busy hours

content.text: If pages load fine in the morning but crawl during a sale, a campaign or the evening rush, your site has hit the limits of its current resources. Cloud hosting lets you add CPU and RAM for those busy periods instead of watching visitors leave.

blocks.text: 2. Traffic spikes catch you by surprise

content.text: A post that goes viral, a sale, or a mention on a big page can multiply your visitors in an hour. On shared hosting, a spike like that can take the site down. On cloud hosting, resources can grow to meet the spike and the site stays up.

A store with more products, more orders and more checkout traffic needs more than a starter plan. Cloud hosting gives a WooCommerce store room to grow without a rebuild, and keeps checkout fast when orders pile up.

blocks.text: 4. Downtime costs you money or trust

content.text: A business site that takes bookings, a store that takes orders, or a service portal your customers rely on cannot afford to be offline. Cloud hosting is built around failover and a 99.99% uptime guarantee, so a single hardware fault does not take your site down.

If you have already moved from Starter to Standard to Business and the site still needs more, the next step is not another shared plan. It is a hosting type with dedicated resources and room to scale, which is what cloud hosting is for.

blocks.text: 6. You run a business application, not just a website

content.text: Customer portals, booking systems, school or clinic software, and other web applications need steady resources and reliable uptime. Cloud hosting fits them better than shared hosting, because the resources are dedicated to your application.

blocks.text: When you do NOT need cloud hosting

content.text: Cloud hosting is not the right first step for everyone. A new blog, a small business website, a portfolio or a shop that is just starting will run well on shared hosting. The Starter plan at Rs 1,499 per year includes 1 website, 20 GB NVMe storage, free SSL, free cPanel, daily backups and free migration, which is everything a new site needs. Paying for cloud hosting before your site needs it is spending money on capacity that will sit unused.

The honest test is traffic and growth. If your site gets a few hundred visitors a day and loads fast, stay on shared hosting. If it regularly slows down, outgrows plan after plan, or loses sales during spikes, that is the moment to move. See

content.text: Moving is free at ZedgeHost, because free website migration is included in every plan. Order the cloud plan that fits your site, then ask support to move the site for you.
